Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMModelTest.testAxisFollowing (actually located in XMLModelTestCase.testAxisFollowing). It asserts:
  - assertXPathPointer(context, "//location[2]/following::node()[2]", "/vendor[1]/product[1]")

- Expected XPath behavior:
  - The following axis selects all nodes in document order after the context node (excluding descendants).
  - The node() test should match any node type (elements, text, comments, PIs, etc.). Thus, the first following node after //location[2] can be a text node (e.g., whitespace), making node()[2] the next node, which is the element /vendor[1]/product[1].

- Actual implementation in the DOM model:
  - In org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node, NodeTest), for NodeTypeTest with type Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE, the code returns true only for Node.ELEMENT_NODE or Node.DOCUMENT_NODE:
    - case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
      return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
  - This excludes text, CDATA, comment, and processing instruction nodes from matching node(), which contradicts XPath semantics.

- Impact on the test:
  - Because node() ignores non-element/document nodes, the first following text node after //location[2] is skipped.
  - Consequently, node()[2] is computed as the second element node, not the second node overall, causing the pointer to resolve to a different node than /vendor[1]/product[1] and making the assertion fail.

- Parallel issue in the JDOM model:
  - In org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.jdom.JDOMNodePointer.testNode(...), for Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE, it similarly restricts matches to Element or Document, exhibiting the same incorrect behavior.

Conclusion:
- The failure is caused by incorrect handling of node() tests in both DOMNodePointer and JDOMNodePointer. For Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE, the implementation should match all node types (i.e., effectively return true), not just elements and documents.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
